topics.title: Native controls
topics.when: Adding or touching any form control, dropdown, select, date or time picker, file upload, slider, colour input, checkbox, radio, tooltip, confirm/alert dialog, scrollable area or menu.

topics.title: Design tokens
topics.when: Starting a UI, creating the theme or global stylesheet, or about to type a colour, pixel value, radius, shadow, z-index or duration into a component.

topics.title: Typography
topics.when: Choosing or loading fonts, setting up the type scale, styling headings or body text, or laying out numbers and tables.

topics.title: Spacing and layout
topics.when: Laying out a page or section, setting padding, margin or gap, building cards, lists, grids, sidebars or page containers.

topics.title: AI-slop blocklist
topics.when: Designing a landing page, hero, feature section, dashboard, card grid or any new visual direction; choosing backgrounds, gradients, shadows, icons or decorative elements.

topics.title: Component states
topics.when: Building any interactive element (button, link, input, row, tab, card action) or any view that loads, lists, saves or deletes data.

topics.title: Forms
topics.when: Building or editing any form, input, sign-in or sign-up screen, settings page, search box, filter bar or inline edit.

topics.title: Responsive design
topics.when: Building any page layout, navigation, table, grid or overlay; before declaring a page done on desktop; whenever fixed widths or heights are being set.

topics.title: Dark mode
topics.when: Defining colour tokens, adding a theme switch, or styling any surface, border, shadow, image or chart that must work on a dark background.

topics.title: Accessibility
topics.when: Building any interactive component, choosing text or border colours, adding images or icons, handling focus, writing custom widgets, or reviewing a page before completion.

topics.title: Motion
topics.when: Adding transitions, animations, hover effects, page or overlay entrances, loading indicators or scroll effects.

topics.title: Colour
topics.when: Creating or changing the palette, choosing a primary or accent colour, colouring status, charts, badges or backgrounds.

topics.title: Finishing details
topics.when: Setting up the document head or root layout, adding images, toasts, modals or overlays, creating error pages, or preparing a project for review or launch.

topics.title: Copy and microcopy
topics.when: Writing any text a user will read - headings, button labels, form labels, error messages, empty states, toasts, placeholder data, meta descriptions.

topics.title: Brand intake
topics.when: Starting UI work in a project for the first time, starting a new product, page or redesign, or whenever design.md is missing or does not answer a design question.

topics.title: Self-audit gate
topics.when: Before reporting any UI task as done, before opening a pull request that touches UI, or when asked to review or audit an interface.

topics.title: Data tables
topics.when: Showing rows of records (lists of users, orders, invoices, logs, search results), building an admin screen or dashboard table, or adding sorting, filtering, selection or pagination to one.

topics.title: Charts and data visualisation
topics.when: Adding a chart, graph, sparkline, KPI tile with a trend, gauge or any visual summary of numbers to a dashboard, report or landing page; choosing a chart library or its colours.

topics.title: Navigation and page structure
topics.when: Building the app shell, header, sidebar, tabs, breadcrumbs or page header; adding a new page or route; deciding where a page's title and main actions go.

topics.title: Icons
topics.when: Adding, choosing or sizing an icon; building icon buttons, navigation items, badges, empty states or status messages with icons; importing an icon library or inline SVG.

topics.title: Internationalisation and right-to-left
topics.when: The product is or will be translated, supports right-to-left languages (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu), shows dates, numbers, currencies or plurals, or sets fixed widths on text.

topics.title: UX laws
topics.when: Designing any screen, flow or navigation; placing primary actions; deciding how many options, steps or fields to show; building multi-step forms, checkouts or onboarding; reviewing a page for usability before calling it done.

topics.title: Visual hierarchy
topics.when: Laying out any page, section, card, dashboard or detail view; styling headings, labels, values and secondary text; deciding what a screen should draw the eye to first; reviewing a screen that looks flat, busy or "all the same".

topics.title: Launch assets
topics.when: Starting UI work in a project, doing the brand intake, setting up the document head or root layout, adding images, logos or icons, or preparing a site or app for review or launch.

topics.title: Landing pages and conversion
topics.when: Building a marketing site, landing page, homepage, hero, pricing or feature page, or a signup, lead or waitlist form.

topics.title: Activation and first run
topics.when: Building what a new user sees after signup (first run, onboarding, setup checklist, tours), empty screens, invite flows, or the home screen for returning users.

NC-02.title: Date and time inputs use the project's picker, not the browser's

NC-03.title: File inputs are hidden behind a styled trigger or dropzone

NC-05.title: Colour inputs use a themed picker

NC-06.title: Checkboxes, radios and switches use tokens

NC-11.title: Dropdowns and selects: anatomy and behaviour

TK-01.title: No hard-coded colours outside the token file

TK-02.title: No Tailwind arbitrary values for spacing, type, radius or z-index

TK-03.title: Semantic colour utilities, not the raw palette

TK-04.title: Spacing values are on the 4px scale

TK-05.title: A token file exists and is complete

TK-07.title: Name tokens by role, in two layers

TK-08.title: Reuse the token; do not mint near-duplicates

TY-02.title: The font is chosen for this product, not by habit

TY-03.title: Fonts load without invisible text or layout shift

TY-05.title: A real type scale with few sizes

TY-06.title: Line height and line length are set for reading

TY-08.title: Weight, tracking and case are used sparingly

SP-01.title: One spacing scale, used for everything

SP-02.title: The same component always has the same padding

SP-03.title: Space shows relationship: inside less than outside

SP-05.title: Content has a maximum width and a gutter

SL-05.title: Glass is an exception, not a surface style

ST-01.title: Every interactive element has hover, focus-visible, active and disabled

ST-03.title: Empty states explain and offer the next action

ST-04.title: Errors are shown where they happen, with a way forward

ST-06.title: Optimistic updates for cheap, reversible actions

ST-07.title: Selected, current and pressed are visible and exposed

FM-01.title: Every input has a visible label

FM-02.title: Inputs declare type, autocomplete and input mode

FM-04.title: Error messages sit under the field and say how to fix it

FM-05.title: Field width matches the expected answer

FM-06.title: Mark optional fields; ask for less

FM-08.title: Submitting shows progress and cannot repeat

RS-01.title: The viewport meta tag is present

RS-02.title: No fixed widths wider than a phone

RS-04.title: The mobile layout is designed, not shrunk

RS-08.title: Fluid media, viewport units and safe areas

DM-01.title: Dark values are defined for the tokens

DM-05.title: The dark palette is designed, not derived

AX-01.title: A visible focus ring on everything focusable

AX-02.title: Never remove an outline without replacing it

AX-04.title: Interactive things are real interactive elements

MO-07.title: Layout stays stable while things move

MO-08.title: Page and view changes use view transitions

CO-01.title: Build the palette from the brand colour

CO-02.title: A tinted neutral scale does most of the work

CO-03.title: Semantic colours have fixed meanings and full pairs

CO-05.title: Data colours are a designed set

CO-06.title: Check every pair, in both themes

FD-02.title: Title and description on every page

FD-07.title: Toasts are placed, timed and stacked

FD-11.title: Content resilience: long, short, many, none

CP-02.title: No filler names, labels or sample data

CP-05.title: Errors say what happened and what to do

BR-03.title: Ask for what is missing, with options

BR-06.title: Record what kind of product it is

SA-01.title: No UI task is done without the audit

SA-05.title: Report with the score and the gaps

DT-02.title: Columns are aligned by what they hold

DT-04.title: The header stays and rows have a set density

DT-07.title: Selection and row actions are predictable

DT-08.title: Long and missing values are handled

CH-02.title: Colour comes from chart tokens and means something

CH-06.title: Charts have states and fit their box

NV-01.title: The current location is always marked

NV-05.title: Links go places, buttons do things

NV-06.title: View state lives in the URL

NV-07.title: The menu is short and grouped

IC-01.title: Icon size follows the text beside it

IC-03.title: Decorative icons are hidden; meaningful ones have text

IN-01.title: Logical properties, not left and right

IN-03.title: Direction and language are declared; direction-aware icons flip

IN-04.title: Format with Intl, pluralise with rules

IN-06.title: Fonts and line height cover every script

UX-01.title: Fitts's law: important targets are big and close

UX-03.title: Jakob's law: follow the conventions people already know

UX-05.title: Von Restorff effect: one thing stands out

UX-06.title: Gestalt: things that look alike behave alike

UX-07.title: Serial position: first and last are remembered

UX-09.title: Goal-gradient and Zeigarnik: show progress toward the goal

UX-10.title: Postel's law: accept input the way people type it

UX-11.title: Tesler's law: the product absorbs the complexity

UX-12.title: Peak-end rule: design the best moment and the ending

VH-01.title: Each view has one focal point

VH-02.title: Levels differ enough to be seen

VH-04.title: Values are louder than their labels

VH-05.title: Layout follows how the page is scanned

AS-01.title: Take an asset inventory and ask for what is missing

LP-01.title: The hero says what, for whom, and what to do

LP-02.title: One goal per page, asked for at every decision point

LP-03.title: Proof sits next to the claim

LP-05.title: Pricing is easy to choose from

LP-06.title: Answer the objections before they leave

LP-07.title: Legal and contact links are present

LP-08.title: Lead forms ask for as little as possible

AC-01.title: The first screen is designed for a new account

AC-03.title: A setup checklist for the rest

AC-04.title: Empty states show the way forward

AC-06.title: Invite and share when there is something to share

AC-07.title: Returning users land where they left off
